subject: Larkspur production latency & error surge — RCA and corrective playbook

Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@larkspur.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: production latency spikes + 500 errors (since 04:30 PDT)

Naomi —

We started seeing sustained latency spikes and a higher 500 error rate against our inference endpoints starting ~04:30 PDT this morning. P95 for generate calls jumped from ~220ms to 1.2s, and error rate climbed to ~7% for a 30-minute window (attached are logs and a sample request ID list). Impacted routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream.

This is affecting customer-facing features for our mobile app — several customers have reported timeouts. We're opening an incident on our side but wanted to alert Redwood immediately and request exec-level attention if needed. Can you share an initial triage plan and ETA for mitigation?

Attachments: larkspur-prod-20270429-logs.tar.gz (log/zip)

Thanks,
Aditi Shah
Head of Platform — Larkspur.ai
aditi@larkspur.ai

Thanks for the heads up, Aditi — I see the logs you attached. We're standing up an internal bridge now and will loop in engineering and SRE. Initial plan: 1) isolate traffic to a warm standby pool, 2) enable increased replica counts for the affected fleet, 3) temporarily disable the new quantized variant if it's in the routing mix, 4) collection of diagnostic traces and KV-cache metrics.

Karthik and Grace are joining the bridge and will lead triage. I will keep you updated on every step and share a short RCA and an action tracker within 24 hours.

—Naomi
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Larkspur outage triage notes and preliminary root cause

Short summary of what we observed on the bridge (notes):
- Time window: 04:28–05:05 PDT saw sharp P95/P99 increase and 5–9% 500s on generate/chat routes.
- Immediate mitigations we applied: routed Larkspur to a warm standby pool (reduced error rate to ~1.3%), increased replica count from 3 -> 6 for the affected autoscaling group, disabled the vq-quantized-8 variant from routing.

Preliminary RCA hypothesis (confirmed by traces & KV metrics):
1) A recent rollout of quantized kernels (vq-quantized-8) introduced a path that increases per-request memory pressure for certain prompt shapes (longer prefix + structured function calls).
2) That path caused higher-than-expected KV cache eviction rates under bursts (we saw eviction spikes at the same timestamps as the 500s).
3) Autoscaler reacted to the CPU profile too slowly (race between scale decisions and burst), producing transient under-provisioning for a short window.

Immediate action items (we executed most during the bridge):
- Rollback quantized variant routing for Larkspur (done).
- Temporarily increase min replicas and warm standby for their pool (done).
- Add a short-circuit circuit breaker for requests that exceed 2x baseline token length to avoid filling the KV cache.
- Collect and attach logs/traces (see attachment from the bridge).

Next steps for full remediation (tracked in action tracker):
- Kernel teams to review quantized scheduling heuristics (owner: Jonas).
- Autoscaler tuning: shorten decision window for short bursts (owner: Kimberly).
- Load testing for those prompt shapes + function-calling flows (owner: Grace).

I'll assemble a concise RCA doc and an action tracker for Naomi to share with Larkspur within 12–18 hours.

-karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-30T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Larkspur incident — interim RCA and proposed corrective playbook

Aditi — thanks again for your patience. Attached is a short RCA and the initial action tracker (PDF + spreadsheet). Summary below:

What happened (short):
- A new quantized kernel variant introduced a scheduling path that increased per-request memory pressure for certain request shapes (long prompts + function-calls). During a traffic burst this caused elevated KV-cache evictions, which in combination with autoscaler latency produced a brief under-provisioning window and elevated 500s.

What we did (immediate):
- Removed the quantized variant from routing for Larkspur.
- Scaled the pool and enabled warm standbys.
- Put a temporary circuit-breaker for abnormally long requests.

Planned corrective actions and timelines (owners):
- Kernel scheduling fix & regression tests (Jonas) — targeted deploy 2027-05-04.
- Autoscaler decision-window tuning and burst tests (Kimberly) — targeted 2027-05-03.
- Load test matrix for function-calling prompts (Grace) — in progress, results due 2027-05-02.
- Update routing policy to prefer warm pools for accounts with tight latency SLOs (Product & Runtime) — Q2 cadence.

We attached: 20270430-larkspur-rca.pdf and 20270501-larkspur-action-tracker.xlsx (action owner rows and dates). We'll run an executive readout on Monday and can invite your engineering leadership.

Please let me know if this aligns with your expectation for remediation cadence. We'll keep the temporary mitigations in place until the kernel/autoscaler changes ship and pass the regression tests.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Customer Reliability

Aditi — thanks for joining the readout today and for the questions. To recap the commitments and status:

- Temporary mitigations remain active (no routing to vq-quantized-8; warm standby enabled) and we've kept their pool at elevated replica counts through 2027-05-04 deploy.
- Kernel scheduling fix was deployed to canary on 2027-05-03 and passed the regression tests in our canary environment; full rollout scheduled for 2027-05-04 morning (Jonas).
- Autoscaler tuning merged; burst simulation showed <0.5% 500s in repeated tests (Kimberly).
- Action tracker was updated during the meeting; link to the tracker and tickets below.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4821, https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-9876

Appreciate your partnership — please reach out to me directly if anything else pops up.
